seo.title: Search Console Users and Permissions Guide
seo.meta_description: How to add owners and users in Google Search Console, what each permission can do and how to keep control of your data, for Orange County businesses.

h1: Search Console Users and Permissions: Keep Control of Your Data
answer: Search Console users and permissions decide who can see and change your property. Owners have full control; full users can view all data and take some actions; restricted users have simple view rights. Only owners can add users, and a property needs at least one verified owner. Anaheim and Orange County businesses should keep ownership in-house and give agencies user access.
key_takeaways: Verified and delegated owners have the same permissions.
Full and restricted users have view rights.
Only owners can add or remove users.
A property can have up to 100 non-owners.

sections.heading: Why permissions matter
sections.body_html: Search Console shows sensitive information about your site and lets owners take actions such as submitting sitemaps or removing URLs. Giving each person the right level of access, and keeping ownership with the business, protects your site when staff or agencies change.

sections.heading: The roles
sections.body_html:
• Owner: full control; can add and remove users, change settings, view all data and use all tools.
  • Full user: view rights to all data and can take some actions.
  • Restricted user: simple view rights on most data.
  • Associate: can act on behalf of the site for certain tasks but can't open Search Console data directly.

sections.heading: Verified vs delegated owners
sections.body_html: Google says both have the same permissions. A verified owner proved ownership with a token, such as an HTML file on the site. A delegated owner was granted ownership by another owner without a token. To remove a verified owner, you remove their token from the site.

sections.heading: At least one verified owner
sections.body_html: Google says a property must have at least one verified owner, or no users will have access. If your only verified owner leaves, verify ownership yourself to keep or regain access.

sections.heading: How to add a user
sections.body_html:
1. Open the property and go to Settings, then Users and permissions (visible only to owners).
  2. Select Add user.
  3. Enter the person's Google Account email.
  4. Choose the permission level and save.

sections.heading: Limits to know
sections.body_html: Google says a property can have up to 100 non-owners. Delegated owners can be added until the property reaches 500 verified plus delegated owners. Users need a valid Google Account; email groups can't be added.

sections.heading: What restricted users can't do
sections.body_html: Google's permissions table shows that actions such as submitting sitemaps and requesting reconsideration are limited to owners and, for some actions, full users. Give restricted access to people who only need to read reports.

sections.heading: Taking over a site
sections.body_html: If you take over a site from another owner, Google says that after verifying ownership you can remove previous owners by removing their verification token, such as the HTML tag they added.

sections.heading: Who should have what
sections.body_html:
• Business owner: verified owner.
  • Marketing manager: full user or delegated owner.
  • Agency: full user, rarely owner.
  • Staff who read reports: restricted user.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Letting an agency be the only verified owner.
  • Leaving former staff with access.
  • Making everyone an owner.
  • Removing the verification token during a redesign and losing access.
  • Sharing one Google login between people.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask how to get access when a former agency won't respond. Verify ownership yourself with a new method, then remove the old owner's token. Another question is whether to give an agency owner access. Full user access is usually enough; keep ownership in the business. Owners also ask whether Search Console access is linked to Google Business Profile access. They're separate, so review both.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• A business account is a verified owner.
  • Agency added as a full user.
  • Former staff removed.
  • Restricted access for read-only staff.
  • Access list reviewed quarterly.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a pool service company in Mission Viejo whose former web developer is the only verified owner. The owner adds a DNS record to verify a Domain property in the company's own account, then removes the developer's old HTML verification file. The company adds its new marketing agency as a full user and its office manager as a restricted user.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: It helps to see where this sits in the bigger picture. Google ranks local results mainly on relevance, distance and popularity, and AI assistants lean on the same public information: your Business Profile, your website, other listings and what customers write. For a business in Anaheim or anywhere in Orange County, the most reliable plan is simple and repeated: keep every listing accurate, explain each service clearly on its own page, show real proof of your work and reply to customers. Small improvements here compound, and they are far harder for competitors to copy than an ad budget.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Open Users and permissions.
  2. Confirm a business account is a verified owner.
  3. Remove anyone who no longer needs access.
  4. Set the right level for each user.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Plenty of owners handle this themselves. Outside help pays off when time is short, when the business has many locations or when a problem is costing calls every day it stays unresolved. Be wary of anyone who promises guaranteed positions or asks for your verification codes or passwords; Google says nobody can pay for a better local ranking. Look for clear explanations, honest timelines and reporting tied to real enquiries. Chimera offers exactly that to businesses in Anaheim and across Orange County.

sections.heading: A quarterly access check
sections.body_html: Put a short access review in the calendar every three months. Open Settings, then Users and permissions, and read down the list. For each person, ask whether they still work with the business and whether they need their current level of access. Remove anyone who has left and lower access for people who only read reports. Check that at least one verified owner is an account controlled by the business, not by an individual or an outside provider, and that you know how that verification works, for example the DNS record or HTML file that proves it. If your site is being rebuilt, warn the developer not to remove verification files or tags without checking. Do the same review for related tools at the same time, including your Google Business Profile, Google Analytics, your website admin and your domain registrar, so access stays consistent. Keep a short written record of who has which role and why, and update it whenever you change access. If you work with an agency, put in the contract that the business remains the verified owner and that agency access ends when the work ends. Ten minutes a quarter prevents the most common problem we see with Orange County businesses: important data and settings controlled by someone who has moved on.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Keep at least one verified owner inside the business, give others the lowest level they need and review the list regularly. Chimera, based in Anaheim, works as a user on Orange County clients' Search Console, never as sole owner.

faqs.q: What permissions does Search Console have?
faqs.a: Owner, full user, restricted user and associate.

faqs.q: What if my only verified owner leaves?
faqs.a: Verify ownership yourself to keep or regain access.

faqs.q: How many users can a property have?
Can I add an email group?
faqs.a: No. Users need a valid Google Account.

faqs.q: Should my agency be an owner?
faqs.a: Usually a full user is enough; keep ownership in the business.

faqs.q: Do you help businesses in Anaheim and Orange County with this?
faqs.a: Yes. Chimera is based in Anaheim, California and works with businesses across Orange County, California.
